title: Decision-dependency ledger

stages.name: extractDecisions
stages.algorithm: Segment meetings at topic boundaries; distinguish a suggestion, assent, and an authorized resolution. Link explicit objections and preserve the speaker rather than attributing a collective decision from an unchallenged statement.
stages.gate: No accepted resolution without attributable acceptance and scope evidence.

stages.name: bindAssumptions
stages.algorithm: For each decision ask what would have to change to make reconsideration necessary. Separate essential premises from background rationale; emit a directed dependency with a counterfactual explanation and a passage establishing the connection.
stages.gate: Every edge has source support; inferred edges remain proposals until owner review.

stages.name: assessChange
stages.algorithm: Compare old and new assertions under their dates, scope, and authority. Determine which premise is actually invalidated and retain the part of the decision whose conditions still hold; never treat a synonym edit as a substantive reversal.
stages.gate: Exact interval overlap plus semantic premise contradiction, not keyword overlap alone.

stages.name: planReconsideration
stages.algorithm: Traverse only necessary dependencies first, then inspect supporting edges for materiality. Group reviews sharing an unresolved premise, formulate a decision-ready question, and avoid automatically cancelling downstream work that remains independently justified.
stages.gate: No dependency cycle silently flattened; each affected owner receives one deduplicated task.

stages.name: recordResolution
stages.algorithm: Reconcile owner responses against the pending question and current evidence version. Distinguish approval of wording from approval of the decision; append the adopted resolution and invalidate only consumers of the replaced version.
stages.gate: Signed owner authority and expected version must match before commit.

operational_details: A decision owner leaves: retain the historical author and route new reviews through an explicit successor assignment.
A private source supports a public decision: expose a restricted-evidence marker, never a revealing excerpt.
Two reviews finish concurrently: reject the stale resolution and show the intervening change rather than overwriting.
A renamed project receives copied notes: keep identity mapping separate from evidence independence.
A meeting correction arrives late: retain both recorded and effective dates and reopen only the affected interval.
representative_episode: A launch depends on a supplier certification; an amendment invalidates only the European scope while an unrelated pricing note changes.
independent_truth_basis: Hidden premise graph, authority assignments, scoped change events, and exact expected reopen set; human review for inferred necessity.
